cases.sentence: Я слышал много подобного, вы все жалкие ___.
cases.explain: Утешители is the predicate nominative after the verb 'are', requiring nominative case.

cases.sentence: Я бы мог говорить так, как вы, если бы вы были на моем ___.
cases.explain: The preposition на (in/at) indicating position governs the prepositional case.

cases.sentence: Ты схватил меня, во свидетельство против ___ самого.
cases.explain: The preposition против (against) governs the genitive case.

cases.sentence: Бог терзает меня в ___, он ненавидит меня.
cases.explain: The preposition в (in) indicating the state or manner governs the prepositional case.

cases.sentence: Враг мой следит зорко и неотступно за ___.
cases.explain: The preposition за (for/after) with the meaning 'watching' governs the instrumental case.

cases.sentence: Люди открывают ___, издеваются надо мной, бьют меня по щекам.
cases.explain: The transitive verb открывают (open) takes the direct object in the accusative case.

cases.sentence: Я шил для себя рубище и лбом своим уткнулся в ___.
cases.explain: The transitive verb уткнулся (pushed) takes the direct object in the accusative case.

cases.sentence: О, как человек защищает в суде своего ___!
cases.explain: The transitive verb защищает (defends) takes the direct object in the accusative case.

reading.ru: Я слышал много подобного, вы все жалкие утешители.
reading.question: What does Job say about his friends?
options: They are miserable comforters who offer poor counsel
reading.correct: They are miserable comforters who offer poor counsel
reading.explain: Job says Я слышал много подобного, вы все жалкие утешители — 'I have heard many such things. You are all miserable comforters!'

reading.ru: Я бы мог говорить так, как вы, если бы вы были на моем месте.
reading.question: What does Job say he could do if the positions were reversed?
options: He could speak against them and criticize them as they criticize him
reading.correct: He could speak against them and criticize them as they criticize him
reading.explain: Job says he could speak against them and shake his head at them if they were in his position of suffering.

reading.ru: О, как ты меня изнурил, ты погубил всех моих домашних.
reading.question: What does Job accuse God of doing to him?
options: God has exhausted him and destroyed all his household
God has blessed him with wealth
reading.correct: God has exhausted him and destroyed all his household
reading.explain: Job laments О, как ты меня изнурил, ты погубил всех моих домашних — 'You have surely worn me out. You have made all my company desolate.'

reading.ru: Восстает на меня худоба моя, и против меня свидетельствует.
reading.question: What does Job say his emaciation does?
options: It testifies against him as evidence of his suffering
reading.correct: It testifies against him as evidence of his suffering
reading.explain: Job says Восстает на меня худоба моя, и против меня свидетельствует — 'My leanness rises up against me. It testifies to my face.'

reading.ru: Бог терзает меня в гневе, он ненавидит меня, он скрижещет на меня зубами.
reading.question: How does Job describe God's treatment of him?
options: God tears him in anger, hates him, and gnashes teeth at him
reading.correct: God tears him in anger, hates him, and gnashes teeth at him
reading.explain: Job says Бог терзает меня в гневе, он ненавидит меня, он скрижещет на меня зубами — 'He has torn me in his wrath and persecuted me. He has gnashed on me with his teeth.'

reading.ru: Люди открывают рты, издеваются надо мной, бьют меня по щекам, ругаясь.
reading.question: How do people treat Job?
options: They mock him openly, strike his cheeks, and insult him
They show him respect and honor
They seek his wisdom and advice
reading.correct: They mock him openly, strike his cheeks, and insult him
reading.explain: The text describes how Люди открывают рты, издеваются надо мной, бьют меня по щекам, ругаясь — 'People open their mouths and mock me, striking my cheeks and insulting me.'
